lens: Money/credit safety: double-charge / double-authorization / negative-balance / lost-or-duplicated-settlement risk in the ai-control-plane invocation/ledger/budget/credit-admission chain (#162-166) and the settlement outbox (#161), on integration/gse-nova-control-plane-premerge-2026-07-22 at /workspace/wt/wave5-integration.

findings.location: apps/web/lib/ai-control-plane/executor.ts:321-341 (hold taken), grep confirms `deps.credit` referenced nowhere else in the file / repo production paths
findings.summary: The executor-level CreditAuthorizationPort.authorizeAndReserve() hold is taken at step 6.6/7.5 and its handle is discarded — no settleProvisional/reconcile/release call exists for it anywhere in executor.ts, internal.ts, or any production call path, and it duplicates a second, independent per-route reservation system in invocation-pipeline.ts/credit-admission.ts.
findings.failureScenario: Currently dormant because sealedProductionExecutor() wires credit: failClosedCreditAuthorizationPort (executor.ts:529), which always throws, so CONFIRMED_CREDITS_ONLY never reaches dispatch in production today. But the moment a real (non-throwing) NOVA-backed adapter is wired to the `credit:` field — explicitly described in the branch's own comments as the very next step (S5) — every CONFIRMED_CREDITS_ONLY invocation will: (1) take a full worst-case-cost hold via deps.credit.authorizeAndReserve, (2) never settle or release it on any outcome (success, clean failure, or thrown error), while (3) invocation-pipeline.ts's separate per-route CreditAuthorizationPort (credit-admission.ts) independently authorizes/settles/releases its own holds against the same grant for the same request. This permanently strands the full worst-case hold at the executor layer on every single invocation (unrecoverable — credit-port.ts has no sweeper), driving the credit grant's apparent spendable balance toward zero/negative even though no money was actually spent that many times, and causing legitimate future dispatches to be wrongly refused insufficient-headroom. This is a previously-identified-and-fixed defect: commit 58ea76e4 on branch feat/ai-control-plane-credit-admission, titled in part 'Executor credit-hold leak (major, inherited from the budgets base): authorizeAndReserve was the port's only call site — every outcome left the reservation HELD forever,' fixes exactly this and also collapses the duplicate reservation system. Verified via `git merge-base --is-ancestor 58ea76e4 HEAD` = NO in the wave5 worktree — the fix commit exists on the source PR branch but was never merged/re-synced into this integration branch (wave5 merged 9b16ef56, an earlier point on that branch).
findings.confidence: High — verified by direct code read (no settle/release call site exists anywhere for this reservation), a repo-wide grep, and a diff against the actual named fix commit which adds the missing settle/release/quarantine lifecycle and removes the duplicate reservation layer.

findings.summary: Credit worst-case authorization and settlement amounts are computed via floating-point `Math.round(plan.maxVendorCashUsd * 100)` instead of the codebase's own exact-decimal (usdToMicros/BigInt) convention used everywhere else money is handled (budget.ts).
findings.failureScenario: For a maxVendorCashUsd value with more than 2 decimal places or one that lands near an IEEE-754 representation boundary, Math.round(x*100) can produce a minor-units figure off by ±1 from the true cap. Both the authorize call (line 561) and the settle call (line 717) recompute the same float expression independently, so they stay self-consistent (not itself a double-charge vector), but it is a real precision gap versus the exact-decimal invariant budget.ts enforces everywhere else, and would need fixing before this credit path becomes reachable in production.
findings.confidence: Medium-high on the defect existing as written; low practical impact today since this code path shares the same fail-closed gating as Finding 1 and is not reachable in production yet.

lens: Idempotency and concurrency: races, non-atomic check-then-act, missing unique/serializable constraints in claim/reservation/authorization code paths on integration/gse-nova-control-plane-premerge-2026-07-22 (worktree /workspace/wt/wave5-integration, HEAD 61270eae)

findings.summary: The budget-hold safety-net sweeper releases a reservation based only on ai_attempts status evidence, without checking whether the owning invocation's own execution lease is still live — it cannot distinguish 'process crashed before dispatching' from 'still RUNNING and about to dispatch the next fallback route.'
findings.failureScenario: Invocation A reserves a $60 hold (expiresAt = now+15min, DEFAULT_HOLD_TTL_MS in invocation-pipeline.ts:239) against a $100-cap window. Its permitted-route walk (invocation-pipeline.ts:535-838) hits several providers that fail cleanly (status FAILED, not TIMEOUT/AMBIGUOUS/DISPATCHED/SUCCEEDED) but slowly, so more than 15 minutes elapse before the next route's startAttempt() call. During that gap the invocation row is RUNNING with zero attempts in the possiblyCharged set, so mustHold is false. A sweepExpired pass landing in that gap releases A's hold (reservedUsd -= 60) and marks it EXPIRED, while A is still alive with a live lease and is about to call startAttempt and actually dispatch a paid call with zero reservation protecting it. Concurrently, Actor B can now reserve() against the freed headroom on the same window. Both A's eventual real charge and B's hold can land, so total exposure on the window exceeds its cap — violating the module's own documented invariant that 'the cap invariant is a database property.' apps/web/__tests__/ai-control-plane-budget.test.ts:906-915 confirms this is the intended-but-flawed model: it seeds an invocation status of RUNNING with the comment '// crashed before any attempt' and asserts release, treating RUNNING+no-evidence as proof of a crash rather than as an ambiguous state that could also mean 'still legitimately working.' Mitigating: grepping apps/web/app for sweepExpired finds no cron route currently invoking it in this branch, so the race is not reachable in production today, but the function's own docstring frames it as the intended crash-recovery safety net meant to run on a schedule, so this becomes live the moment that wiring is added with no other code change required.
findings.confidence: high on the code-level defect (verified by direct reading of budget.ts and its test); medium on present-day exploitability since sweepExpired is not yet wired to any cron in this branch

noFindingsStatement: Not applicable — one finding reported above. All other claim/reservation/authorization paths inspected (budget.ts reserve/settleProvisional/release/holdForReconciliation/confirmSettlement; credit-admission.ts's CreditAuthorizationPort atomic ledger authorize/settle/release, currently dormant/unwired via executor.ts:454-460; control-store.ts claimInvocation/startAttempt lease-fencing; settlement-outbox/worker.ts claimVersion-fenced leases; packages/ingestion-pipeline/src/settle-sport.ts PENDING-scoped exactly-once settlement; billing/checkout-attempt.ts unique-constraint convergence loop; billing/reconcile-entitlements.ts guarded revoke) used correct atomic-guard / state-scoped-update patterns and yielded no concrete concurrent-actor scenario that breaks an invariant.

lens: Authority and authorization: paths where an agent, unauthenticated actor, or lower-privilege actor could take an owner-only or higher-privilege action (mint credits, approve its own work, bypass the trusted-actor model, escalate FounderWorkAuthority).
noFindingsStatement: No real authorization-escalation findings after a genuine, code-level investigation of the Wave 5 integration branch (worktree /workspace/wt/wave5-integration, HEAD 61270eae on integration/gse-nova-control-plane-premerge-2026-07-22). Investigated and verified by reading source (not summaries) and executing real test suites: (1) the TrustedActor boundary in apps/web/lib/auth/actor.ts — HUMAN actors only come from session-derived requireSessionActor/requireAdminActor, SERVICE/SYSTEM actors only from resolveServiceActor() which enforces a hardcoded principal allowlist, a VerifiedCredentialContext, per-principal operation scoping, and mandatory requestId/runId correlation; the raw serviceActor()/systemActor() constructors are deprecated and structurally fenced by scripts/guardrails/actor-minting-boundary.mjs, which I ran directly (node scripts/guardrails/actor-minting-boundary.mjs) and confirmed reports "OK — scanned 1576 files, no raw actor minting outside the boundary" on this branch; (2) apps/web/lib/ai-control-plane/emergency.ts's EmergencyOverrideReceipt verification, which fails closed on missing/expired/revoked/wrong-scope receipts and structurally re-validates (not just type-checks) that approvedByActor is a HUMAN/SESSION/ADMIN actor with a non-empty subjectId — the production receipt store (failClosedReceiptStore) makes EMERGENCY_RELIABILITY unreachable until a durable store ships; (3) apps/web/lib/ai-control-plane/credit-admission.ts's admitCreditFunded/authorize — fail-closed on any store error, missing snapshot, insufficient headroom, or currency mismatch, with authorize() using one atomic conditional UPDATE against a per-grant reservation ledger (no read-then-write race); (4) apps/web/lib/ai-control-plane/validation.ts's resolveEffectiveAuthority — every narrowing field (provider routes, cost modes, cash cap, substitutions, retention) can only shrink what the registry granted (failEscalation on any attempt to widen), and capabilityFloor/dataPolicy/validationPolicy aren't even present in the AiAuthorityNarrowing type, so a caller cannot touch them at all; (5) the NOVA S1-S4 Founder OS / capability-governor / nova-agent modules (founder-command.ts, nova-agent.ts, capability-governor.ts) are genuinely read-only/no-execution — classifyFounderWork is monotonic escalation-only (AGENT_INTERNAL -> AGENT_THEN_OWNER -> OWNER_ONLY, never the reverse) and every exported classification type carries executionAuthority:false; I confirmed apps/web/app/cockpit/nova/founder/page.tsx has no "use server" actions, fetch/POST, or mutation call anywhere in the file, and apps/web/lib/ai-control-plane is imported into exactly one live route (the cron drain endpoint, which is itself bearer-token gated via lib/cron/authorize.ts's constant-time timingSafeEqual compare) — the executor/dispatch/invocation-pipeline is not yet wired to any user- or agent-reachable route in this branch; (6) apps/web/lib/community/moderation-actions.ts's admin-gated actions all call requireAdminActor()/requireSessionActor() before any domain logic. I ran the dedicated authority test suite directly (npx vitest run __tests__/ai-control-plane-authority.test.ts inside apps/web) covering policy-registry completeness, escalation-attack vectors, request validation, and emergency receipts, and all 71 tests passed; I also ran __tests__/council-ledgers.test.ts (48 tests passed) and __tests__/ai-control-plane-credit-admission.test.ts (32 passed, 2 skipped — those 2 require a live Postgres instance not available in this environment, so the "real Postgres concurrent authorize()" claim in the module's docstring could not be independently re-verified here). One sub-finding I evaluated but am not reporting as a real vulnerability: apps/web/lib/jarvis/ledgers-core.ts's reviewSubagentRunAs() calls assertActorType(actor, ["HUMAN"], ...) rather than also checking authorityScope==="ADMIN", which would in principle let a non-admin HUMAN actor review/approve a subagent run if the function were ever called directly with a session (non-admin) actor — but I traced every caller in the repo (grep for reviewSubagentRunAs/logHandoffAs/logSubagentRunAs across apps, packages, workers, scripts) and the only production caller is apps/web/lib/jarvis/ledgers.ts, whose "use server" wrapper calls requireAdminActor() before invoking it; the module's own docblock documents this as intentional design (core module trusts its caller, mirroring the rest of the codebase's layering), and there is no unguarded second call site. This is a latent defense-in-depth gap worth flagging to the team for awareness, not a currently exploitable escalation path, so I have not listed it as a finding. Summary: 0 real findings after genuine investigation.

lens: Secrets and AI transport import boundary (post-Wave-5 cumulative integration, 16 branches merged)

findings.summary: New ai-control-plane dispatch module imports raw AI transport (callClaudeMessages) and all three raw provider clients (bedrock, vertex, cerebras) directly, bypassing the AI transport import-boundary allowlist enforced by scripts/guardrails/ai-transport-import-boundary.mjs.
findings.failureScenario: The file was introduced in commit 1aa0a3ab ('feat(ai-control-plane): authoritative claim/idempotency + exact provider dispatch + attribution constraints (directive §9)'), which entered the integration branch via the PR#164 merge (feat/ai-control-plane-budgets). Neither apps/web/lib/ai-control-plane/dispatch.ts nor any equivalent path was added to PERMANENT_ADAPTER_ALLOWLIST or TRANSITIONAL_ALLOWLIST in scripts/guardrails/ai-transport-import-boundary.mjs. Running `node scripts/guardrails/ai-transport-import-boundary.mjs` on the current worktree HEAD (61270eae) fails with 4 violations at dispatch.ts:33 (raw-transport-import of callClaudeMessages), :34 (raw-provider-import of providers/bedrock), :40 (raw-provider-import of providers/vertex), and :46 (raw-provider-import of providers/cerebras). This check is wired into CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:267, job `ai-transport-import-boundary`) and into the aggregate `npm run guardrails` script (package.json:72), so the integration branch as it currently stands would fail CI on this gate. The guard's own file header explicitly anticipated this case ('joined then by the sealed control-plane executor... once E0 exists') but the allowlist update was never made when the E0 control-plane dispatch code landed. grep found no other file in the repo importing apps/web/lib/ai-control-plane/dispatch.ts, so it is not yet wired into a live request path — meaning this is not an active production data-exfiltration bypass today — but it is a real, currently-failing state of the exact guard this review was asked to verify. If this file is later wired into a live path, raw transport becomes reachable from application code outside the sanctioned adapters with no guard warning unless the allowlist gap is fixed first.
findings.confidence: high — reproduced directly by running the guardrail script against the actual worktree HEAD (61270eae); CI wiring and aggregate script were independently confirmed by grep of .github/workflows/ci.yml and package.json.

findings.summary: The only freshness check on the public picks/board read paths (isPublicPicksSurfaceStale) is itself gated behind gates.forceNoBetIfStale, which defaults to false via FORCE_NO_BET_IF_STALE (parseBool(..., false) at platform-config.ts:175).

lens: Test coverage honesty: credit admission, settlement outbox dead-letter, trusted-actor IP derivation, capability governor fail-closed paths

findings.summary: The dead-letter escalation write's own failure path (db.outboxDeadLetterReceipt.createMany throwing) is never exercised by any test, even though the module's own docs single it out as the durable owner-queue escalation mechanism for DEAD_LETTER deliveries.
findings.failureScenario: appendDeadLetterReceipt (worker.ts:733) wraps db.outboxDeadLetterReceipt.createMany in a try/catch that swallows the error into summary.errors and returns silently (worker.ts:753-755) -- a delivery can be marked DEAD_LETTER while its durable escalation receipt silently fails to write, with no owner ever notified via that channel. worker.test.ts's fake table (`makeTable`, line 150) has no mechanism to simulate a throwing createMany, and no test in the file forces this branch (confirmed via grep: `deadLetterReceipts`/`outboxDeadLetterReceipt` only appear in table setup and in the happy-path dedup assertions at lines 441-445). So nothing verifies: (1) the drain doesn't abort or skip subsequent candidates when this call throws, (2) summary.errors actually captures the failure message, (3) the delivery row still correctly reports DEAD_LETTER despite the escalation-record failure, or (4) a regression where this catch block starts rethrowing (which would blow up the surrounding per-delivery try/catch and could abort the whole delivery loop) or stops swallowing correctly. In production, if the OutboxDeadLetterReceipt table write is ever broken (wrong column, constraint violation, connection blip), deliveries would still show DEAD_LETTER (well covered by tests) but would never surface as a reviewable owner work item -- and the test suite would not catch that regression because the fake store is never configured to fail on this specific call.
findings.confidence: high -- verified by reading worker.ts:733-756 and grepping worker.test.ts for every reference to the dead-letter-receipt table; only the dedup (skipDuplicates) success path is exercised, never a throwing store.

lens: Schema and migration safety (Prisma schema + all new migrations on integration/gse-nova-control-plane-premerge-2026-07-22)

findings.summary: Two independent new migrations in this wave share the identical timestamp prefix 20260722150000, a merge collision from two different feature branches (Trusted Actor Model work and AI Control Plane PR-C budget work) generating migrations at the same minute.
findings.failureScenario: Prisma's migration engine has no numeric-timestamp uniqueness check; it applies migrations in lexical order of the full folder name, so 'add_actor_receipts_and_durable_rate_limits' happens to sort before 'add_ai_budget_reservations' ('c' < 'i') and both currently apply cleanly (verified: no cross-FK dependency between them). But this ordering is accidental, not controlled: a future migration whose folder name sorts lexically between these two, or a rename during a future merge conflict resolution, would silently reorder execution relative to what either author tested, since nothing enforces monotonic timestamps once two prefixes collide. `prisma migrate status`/`migrate diff` output also becomes ambiguous to reason about chronologically once two entries share a timestamp.
findings.confidence: high — verified via `ls` (both directories share the byte-identical '20260722150000' prefix) and by reading both migration.sql files in full.

findings.location: packages/db/prisma/migrations/ (whole directory — earliest migration only ALTERs pre-existing "picks"/"games" tables, no CREATE TABLE baseline) and scripts/deploy/migrate-if-configured.mjs (runs real `prisma migrate deploy` unconditionally when VERCEL_ENV=production)
findings.summary: The migrations directory has no baseline migration for the core schema — the earliest file only ALTERs a table that must already exist — so `prisma migrate deploy` cannot bootstrap a genuinely empty Postgres database from migration history alone; the actual schema shape has only ever been materialized out-of-band via `prisma db push`.
findings.failureScenario: This is not hypothetical: the repo's own scripts/integration/settlement-outbox-acceptance.mjs (lines ~85-94) documents it verbatim as an 'honest limitation, pre-existing in this repo' and works around it by using `prisma db push` instead of `migrate deploy` to materialize schema for its acceptance test. Meanwhile scripts/deploy/migrate-if-configured.mjs runs real `prisma migrate deploy` against the production DB on every VERCEL_ENV=production build. If production's database is ever rebuilt from scratch (disaster recovery, a new region/tenant DB, a Neon branch promoted to prod, or a restore predating the `_prisma_migrations` ledger being seeded), the production migrate-deploy step fails outright on the very first migration in history because the table it ALTERs doesn't exist yet — precisely the outage class that script's own comments say it was hardened against (referencing 'the #70 outage' and a 2026-07-10 fail-closed rollout after the ledger 'silently diverged from the repo for weeks'). This wave adds 9 more migrations on top of the same ungrounded history without addressing the missing baseline.
findings.confidence: high — confirmed via the repository's own code comments admitting the gap (scripts/integration/settlement-outbox-acceptance.mjs), cross-checked against migrate-if-configured.mjs which does run real `migrate deploy` unconditionally in production.

findings.location: .github/workflows/ci.yml lines ~70-73 ('Prisma schema validate' / 'Push database schema (test DB)' steps) vs scripts/integration/settlement-outbox-acceptance.mjs (not referenced in any .github/workflows/*.yml)
findings.summary: The standard CI gate never applies the migrations directory via `prisma migrate deploy`; it only runs `prisma validate` (schema-only, no DB) and `prisma db push` (schema-driven, bypasses the migrations directory and the `_prisma_migrations` history entirely). The one script that applies the real settlement-hardening migration chain end-to-end and proves its idempotency/FK/claim-fencing guarantees — scripts/integration/settlement-outbox-acceptance.mjs — is not wired into any GitHub Actions workflow (grepped every file in .github/workflows/ for its filename: zero hits) or any package.json script; its only mention in the repo is as a catalog entry in reports/nova/convergence/NOVA_CONVERGENCE_INVENTORY.md/.json.
findings.failureScenario: A future edit to 20260722183000_harden_settlement_evidence_outbox/migration.sql or 20260722213000_outbox_dead_letter_receipts/migration.sql — e.g. someone simplifying one of the guarded `DO $$` constraint-swap blocks, or accidentally breaking the IF-NOT-EXISTS re-apply idempotency those files' own comments claim — passes ordinary CI (lint/typecheck/test/db-push) unnoticed, because db-push regenerates schema from schema.prisma directly and never executes these .sql files. The migration comments assert things like 'the acceptance harness proves this' (20260722213000) as though that guarantee is continuously enforced, but nothing in CI actually runs that harness on any push or PR.
findings.confidence: high — confirmed by grepping .github/workflows/ci.yml and every other workflow file for the acceptance script's name and for `migrate deploy`/`migrate dev`: no invocation found; confirmed the only DB-provisioning step in ci.yml's test job is `npm run db:push` → `prisma db push`.

lens: Formal verification soundness: TLA+ specs / property-chaos harness vs. current Wave 5 merged code (formal/, formal-regression/)

findings.location: formal/credit-budget/CreditReservation.tla:93-99 (Settle action + comment) vs apps/web/lib/ai-control-plane/credit-admission.ts:495-517 (real settle()); cross-checked against formal-regression/src/reference/credit-reference.ts:41-43 and formal-regression/src/tests/credit-reservation.real.property.test.ts:111-151
findings.summary: The TLA+ spec's Settle action (and its 'independent oracle' reference-model reimplementation) models a settled reservation as PERMANENTLY occupying the balance ('reserved' stays UNCHANGED — comment: 'a settled charge still occupies the balance it consumed'), but the real, merged createPgCreditAuthorizationPort.settle() does the opposite: it decrements credit_grant_reservation_ledger.reservedMinorUnits by the held amount, identically to release(). This is directly confirmed by the branch's own real-Postgres integration test titled 'settle/release against real Postgres: reserved returns to 0 either way' (apps/web/__tests__/ai-control-plane-credit-admission.test.ts:1089).
findings.failureScenario: I reproduced this directly against the real (unmodified) createPgCreditAuthorizationPort using the formal-regression harness's own fixture adapters: authorize() a $60 hold against a $100 grant (admitted), settle() it for the full $60, then authorize() another $60 hold against the SAME grant — it is admitted a second time, because nothing in credit-admission.ts (or anywhere in the repo — grepped, no hits) ever decrements the grant's remainingMinorUnits on settle; only the transient reservation-ledger row is touched, and settle() frees it back to 0 exactly like a release. A caller settling and re-authorizing in a loop against a static/unrefreshed snapshot (which is exactly what today's merged code has, since no production CreditSnapshotStore exists yet — S5 persistence is still unbuilt) can authorize unbounded multiples of the grant's nominal balance. This is the precise class of bug (NeverOverAdmit / no-double-spend) the TLA+ spec and its flagship property exist to rule out, but the model's Settle semantics do not correspond to what settle() actually does in the code it claims to formalize, so the proof does not cover this real behavior.
findings.confidence: high — verified by direct code read, a real reproduction test run against the unmodified production function, and an existing test in the same branch that independently confirms settle() zeroes the ledger just like release().

findings.location: formal-regression/src/tests/credit-reservation.real.property.test.ts:111 (test title "release() frees headroom for a LATER attempt (settle keeps it consumed)")
findings.summary: This property test's title makes an explicit factual claim ('settle keeps it consumed') mirroring the TLA+ spec's incorrect Settle semantics, but the test body never calls settle() at all — it only exercises release(). The claim in the title is therefore both false (per the finding above) and untested, meaning the property-chaos harness that is supposed to cross-check the formal model against the real implementation has a blind spot precisely where the model and the real code diverge.
findings.failureScenario: A future reviewer or maintainer reads this test title as documentation ('settle keeps it consumed, verified by this suite') and concludes the settle-path double-spend protection is covered, when in fact no test in formal-regression/ or the real-Postgres suite (apps/web/__tests__/ai-control-plane-credit-admission.test.ts) ever asserts that settling reduces available headroom for a later authorize() call against the same snapshot — the only real-Postgres test touching this ('settle/release against real Postgres') affirmatively demonstrates the opposite of what the title here claims.
findings.confidence: high — directly read the test file; confirmed no settle() call exists in that test body.

findings.summary: This branch converts the previously fully-inert watchlist alert seam into a real, cron-driven, autonomous outbound-communication pipeline (live Resend email SDK + live web-push SDK), one flag flip away from sending real messages to real users with no per-send owner approval.
findings.failureScenario: Before this branch, apps/web/lib/watchlist/alert-dispatch.ts documented 'no SMTP/push client dependency exists' and always returned no_channel_wired (zero I/O, zero call sites). This branch adds the `resend` and `web-push` npm packages, wires channels/email-channel.ts to call `new Resend(...).emails.send(...)` and channels/web-push-channel.ts to push real notifications, connects both to a new settlement-hook.ts caller, and registers a brand-new Vercel cron entry `/api/cron/deliver-settlement-alerts` (vercel.json) that fires daily in production automatically once deployed. The only gates preventing real sends today are: (1) `WATCHLIST_ALERTS_ENABLED` env var defaulting to "false" in .env.example, and (2) `RESEND_API_KEY`/`ALERTS_EMAIL_FROM`/VAPID keys being unset. If a founder (or anyone with prod env-var access) sets `WATCHLIST_ALERTS_ENABLED=true` and populates the Resend/VAPID keys — a routine 'turn the feature on' action, not a code change — the already-deployed cron will begin autonomously emailing/push-notifying real users on every settlement run, with no per-batch human approval step (only the boolean flag + per-user entitlement/verified-email checks gate it).
findings.confidence: high that this is new live-send capability added in this branch (verified via package.json diff, live Resend .emails.send() call, live web-push send, new cron route+auth, new vercel.json schedule); medium on whether this counts as 'outreach' in the strict sense the lens targets — these are transactional alerts to already-opted-in, entitled subscribers (Watchlist follow + Elite tier + verified email), not cold outreach to prospects/competitors. It is properly authenticated (CRON_SECRET bearer check in the route) and fail-closed by default (flag off, keys empty in .env.example), and is explicitly documented in the branch's own OWNER_DECISION_PACKET_2026-07-22.md as founder-activated. Reporting it because it is the one concrete case in this diff where dormant/never-wired code became a live external-send capability gated only by an env flag, which is exactly the near-miss pattern requested.

findings.location: apps/web/lib/ai-control-plane/executor.ts:333, executor.ts:460, executor.ts:529; port definitions at apps/web/lib/ai-control-plane/credit-port.ts:59 and apps/web/lib/ai-control-plane/credit-admission.ts:340; self-flagged at apps/web/lib/ai-control-plane/internal.ts:135-146
findings.summary: Two independently-designed, live-wired CreditAuthorizationPort implementations exist for the same CONFIRMED_CREDITS_ONLY admission decision — a whole-plan-level port (credit-port.ts, sealed into the outer executor) and a per-route Postgres-backed port (credit-admission.ts, instantiated with a real DB handle inside productionDispatch) — which is the 'second economic-truth model' pattern the canonical ownership table's 'one economic truth' rule is meant to prevent, even though both paths are currently fail-closed.
findings.failureScenario: Currently inert: the outer port is permanently sealed to the always-throwing failClosedCreditAuthorizationPort (executor.ts:529), and the inner per-route port is gated behind an always-undefined deps.creditStore (invocation-pipeline.ts:504), verified by reading invocation-pipeline.ts:499-528, so CONFIRMED_CREDITS_ONLY fails closed either way today. The real risk is forward-looking: when NOVA's S5 unit wires a real CreditSnapshotStore/adapter (the explicitly-flagged next step in these files' own comments), an engineer could plug it into only one of the two ports while the other remains referenced elsewhere, producing two independently-authorizing credit gates (one whole-plan, one per-route) that can disagree about whether a grant has headroom for the same request — i.e. two competing sources of economic truth, in tension with the freeze §2 / CONSTELLATION 'one economic truth' invariant these same files cite.
findings.confidence: high — verified by direct code read of both ports' full interfaces, both wiring sites in executor.ts, and the fail-closed gate in invocation-pipeline.ts. This is the same collision the branch's own npm run nova:inventory receipt (commit 61270eae) already surfaces as 'the same architecture duplication already flagged as an owner decision during the PR#166 merge commit' — so this confirms a pre-acknowledged, still-unresolved issue on the integration branch rather than a newly hidden one.

noFindingsStatement: Beyond the one credit-authorization duplication above (which the branch's own convergence-inventory tooling had already self-flagged), I found no other role-boundary violations. Specifically verified clean: (1) S4 Founder OS (apps/web/lib/nova/founder-os-dashboard.ts, apps/web/app/cockpit/nova/page.tsx, apps/web/app/cockpit/nova/founder/page.tsx) is the sole owner-decision-queue/cockpit surface for NOVA economics — both pages source from the single loadNovaFounderOsSummary loader over @/lib/opportunity-engine, with zero database writes anywhere in lib/opportunity-engine or lib/nova (grep for prisma/.create(/.update(/.upsert( returned nothing), matching the 'read-models only, no second dashboard' rule stated in founder-command.ts's own header comment. (2) No agent in apps/web/lib/agents/agent-registry.ts claims a NOVA/Founder cockpitSurfacesOwned entry. (3) CreditGrantSnapshot and TrustedActor each have exactly one canonical declaration site (apps/web/lib/opportunity-engine/credit-snapshot.ts:70 and apps/web/lib/auth/actor.ts:210 respectively) — no forked vocabulary. (4) Genesis Kernel (packages/genesis-kernel) is a standalone, fixture-driven offline CLI (plan-cli.ts/scan-cli.ts writing only to tmp/genesis/) not imported by any apps/web route — it does not build a live cockpit, owner queue, or economic model; its internal OWNER_GATE/FOUNDER_GATED vocabulary is a local plan-compiler concept, not a competing owner-decision surface. (5) The pre-existing JARVIS agent-task queue (apps/web/lib/jarvis/jarvis-decision-queue.ts, jarvis-owner-summary.ts) predates this integration branch (already present at origin/main tip c19a00d8) and covers a different domain (engineering/agent-task approvals, not NOVA revenue/economics), so it is not a violation introduced by this wave. (6) The AI control plane never writes CreditGrantSnapshot rows (grep for create/update/upsert on it in lib/ai-control-plane returned nothing), respecting 'written by NOVA-side reconcilers only.' One pre-existing, explicitly-acknowledged parallel budget system (ClaudeApiBudget in packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma:1863, still used by several call sites) coexists with the new AiBudgetWindow model, but this predates the wave and is explicitly documented in docs/ai/phase0/AI_CONTROL_PLANE_DESIGN_2026-07-22.md as an intentional, incremental migration (executeAiTask as a compatibility facade, 'no call site force-migrated'), so I did not count it as a new violation. Summary: 1 real finding (medium severity, pre-acknowledged-but-still-unresolved), ranked above; no other genuine role-boundary violations found after this investigation.
